### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. nonsyndromic genetic hearing loss  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.735)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:2180)

**Proposed mechanism:** GJB2 variant causing dominant-negative effect (rsXXXXXX) —DISRUPTS→ GJB2 (HGNC:2180); GJB2 (HGNC:2180) —DISRUPTS→ Gap junction function (GO:0005887); Gap junction function (GO:0005887) —LEADS_TO→ Familial expansile osteolysis (MONDO:0011058); GJB2 variant causing loss-of-function (rsYYYYYY) —DISRUPTS→ GJB2 (HGNC:2180); GJB2 (HGNC:2180) —DISRUPTS→ Gap junction function (GO:0005887); Gap junction function (GO:0005887) —LEADS_TO→ Nonsyndromic genetic hearing loss (MONDO:0019497). Both Familial expansile osteolysis and nonsyndromic genetic hearing loss are mechanistically linked through the GJB2 gene, which encodes connexin 26. Different types of mutations in GJB2 can lead to distinct functional consequences. Dominant-negative mutations can disrupt normal connexin 26 function, leading to Familial expansile osteolysis. Loss-of-function mutations, on the other hand, impair gap junction communication, resulting in nonsyndromic genetic hearing loss.

**How to falsify it:** If pathogenic variants in GJB2 are not found in individuals with Familial expansile osteolysis, or if these variants do not exhibit dominant-negative effects, this hypothesis would be falsified. **Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis of these two conditions could lead to the development of targeted therapies that modulate GJB2 function or downstream pathways, potentially benefiting patients with either disease. For instance, therapies aimed at restoring gap junction function or mitigating the effects of dominant-negative proteins could be explored.
